💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s possible to see a blockchain transfer within minutes, but that doesn’t mean a casino will process a withdrawal request that fast.
  • When reviewing a crypto casino in Canada, the first step should be to analyze the payment terms and ensure the casino is approved to take your business in your province.
  • Internal approval and blockchain processing are separate steps in a withdrawal request.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s possible to see a blockchain transfer within minutes, but that doesn’t mean a casino will process a withdrawal request that fast. Various factors, including fees and the game being played, impact how quickly a withdrawal can be processed. With that in mind, readers should evaluate claims beyond the headline.

When reviewing a crypto casino in Canada, the first step should be to analyze the payment terms and ensure the casino is approved to take your business in your province. Just because a casino supports crypto payments doesn’t mean it’s licensed to take your business, offers instant payouts, or has games that have been vetted by an independent testing agency. Each of those should be supported by additional evidence.

Internal approval and blockchain processing are separate steps in a withdrawal request.

Look at each step of the withdrawal process in turn. Determine if a guaranteed timeframe covers the entire process or only certain requests.

A payment transaction hash is the best way to trace a payment. Prior to the payment being transmitted, account status or support can give information about the payment processing.

In a recent development, there are several costs associated with a crypto payment that should be taken into consideration. A wallet or exchange may charge a fee to send funds, a blockchain may charge a fee to process the transaction, and the casino may charge a withdrawal fee.

Conversion also needs to be considered. Deposits converted to a Canadian dollar balance need to consider exchange rates, conversion timing, and spread. Leaving funds in cryptocurrency means their Canadian dollar value can change, while the coin balance remains the same.

Look at minimum withdrawals and fees. A small payout can incur a high cost, especially with fixed fees. Promotions can also impact which funds are available for withdrawal.

According to recent reports, evaluate evidence supporting claims of game fairness. Consider how outcomes are determined and whether published rules are implemented. Look for game providers who are independently tested and named, rather than relying on a badge.

A stated return to player is based on the long-term average and does not prohibit large losses.

Some games offer “provably fair” verification. Note what the verification actually checks, and whether you can reproduce the check yourself. Verifying a specific outcome does not mean you can validate withdrawal reliability, the legality of the game, or the security of the components of the game.

Readers from Canada should check their local gambling authority. In Ontario, for example, iGaming Ontario has a directory of licensed operators, and OLG operates separately. Usually, the actual website is more important than recognizing the brand.

According to recent reports, look at account currency and payment totals to determine withdrawal terms. Keep a copy of the terms to show and explain discrepancies to support your case.

It’s notable to assess speed of payout, fees, and fairness of a service separately. Assessing a service by the acceptance of cryptocurrency, in general, is a poor quality standard. It’s important to set limits on time and money spent, and to set funds apart, for example, for gambling, from funds that should be for saving or for daily expenses.

In a recent development, shiba Inu (SHIB) gained 5.96% over the past 24 hours and traded at $0.0000038 on Monday, according to CoinMarketCap, as talk of a December "Santa rally" returned to the crypto market. Still, SHIB is down 8.86% over the past seven days, and the token has lost 18.5% in November so far, according to CryptoRank.

Last week, SHIB dropped to $0.00000337, its lowest level since 2021.

It has been revealed that the hopes for a Santa rally come after Goldman Sachs analysts stated last week that most of the December gains on the stock market usually come after Dec. 15. SHIB's own December history, however, shows that the Santa rally came for the token once in five years.

It has been revealed that according to CryptoRank, SHIB lost 29.5% and 13.5% in December of 2021 and 2022, respectively. In December of 2023, the token gained 24.6%. In December of 2024 and 2025, SHIB lost 21% and 17.6%, respectively.

SHIB's median December return is -17.6%, and its average December return is -11.4%, according to CryptoRank data.

The green December of 2023 came after SHIB gained 6.04% in October and 6.62% in November of that year, according to CryptoRank. In 2026, SHIB lost 18.6% in October, and November is also in the red so far.

The Goldman note, titled "GS Flow of Funds: Chopsgiving," came from Gail Hafif, Brian Garrett and Lee Coppersmith, who looked at S&P 500 data going back to 1928. According to the note, the index usually gains 1.1% from mid-November to early December and then gives back about two-thirds of that gain by mid-December, and around 80% of the full 2.4% gain comes after Dec. 14-15.

Since 1990, the S&P 500 has risen after Dec. 15 in 27 of 36 years, according to Goldman.

The Goldman team called these figures a historical map. In the years when the VIX volatility index was above 18 in the middle of November, the S&P 500 gained 1.34% on average, and the index ended the year higher in 59% of cases, according to the note. According to Goldman, the VIX was above that level in mid-November of this year as well.

Goldman also remarked that retail investors have been buying massive tech and chip stocks. Large funds and systematic traders have been cutting their positions, according to the note.

The Stock Trader's Almanac counts the last five trading days of December and the first two trading days of January as the Santa Claus rally. This season, the window will open on Dec. 24 and close on Jan. 5.

In the window that ended on Jan. 5, 2026, the S&P 500 declined 0.11%, according to the Almanac. "Santa was a no-show for the third year in a row," the Almanac wrote. Before that, the S&P 500 also ended the Santa Claus rally windows of 2023 and 2024 lower.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that NVIDIA added about $1 trillion in market value on Nov. 23 as its shares surged more than 35% after the unexpected reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive.

The rally put the chipmaker on course for the largest single-day market capitalization gain in stock market history, reversing part of the selloff triggered by Huang's resignation less than two weeks earlier.

The Kobeissi Letter noted that NVIDIA's shares initially climbed more than 28%, adding approximately $820 billion to its market capitalization, before extending gains above 35% and pushing the increase past $1 trillion.

If sustained through the closing bell, the increase would establish a upcoming record for the largest amount of market value added by a publicly traded tech giant in a single session.

The gains followed NVIDIA's announcement that its board had unanimously reinstated Huang as president, CEO and director, effective immediately.

Industry observers note that directors said discussions with Huang had satisfied them about his ability to lead the company. The board also consulted senior US government officials before concluding that his reinstatement posed no national security risk.

In a recent development, the decision reversed NVIDIA's Nov. 12 leadership shake-up, which had intensified selling across technology stocks and cryptocurrencies.

The rebound extended beyond NVIDIA, with the Nasdaq advancing more than 6% and the S&P 500 gaining approximately 5% in early trading.

In a recent development, cryptocurrencies also rallied as traders rapidly increased their exposure to riskier assets. Bitcoin surged more than 4% within an hour of the announcement, reaching $64,427 after briefly falling below $60,000 during the previous week's selloff.

However, smaller cryptocurrencies recorded even stronger gains.

Recent findings suggest that glassnode reported that altcoins led the market's initial response to Huang's reinstatement. Within 20 minutes of the announcement, nearly every cryptocurrency among the 50 largest was outperforming Bitcoin.

The analytics firm observed the rally spread from altcoins to the Nasdaq and Bitcoin, while the S&P 500 posted a smaller advance.

The rapid rotation indicated how quickly appetite for speculative assets returned following the leadership reversal at the world's leading AI chipmaker.

The reinstatement also produced a dramatic reversal in prediction-market pricing.

On Nov. 16, CryptoSlate previously reported that Polymarket traders assigned Huang only a 6% probability of returning to NVIDIA by Nov. 30, despite growing pressure from prominent technology executives and investors.

At the time, the probability of a return by Dec. 31 stood at 14%, while the longer-dated contract covering December 2027 carried a 38% probability.

However, those expectations changed significantly following NVIDIA's announcement. By Nov. 23, the November contract had climbed to 99.3%, before reaching 100% on Polymarket's market page.

Combined trading volume across the four contracts reached approximately $12.34 million, reflecting heightened interest in the leadership crisis.

Two quotes on the same Polymarket contract for a formal return to NVIDIA.

Huang’s executive roles and board seat qualify under the event rules.

The bars compare two dated observations.

It has been revealed that both bars use the same zero-based 0% to 100% scale. Length is proportional to the reported Yes quote. The dated points come from CryptoSlate’s Nov. 16 article and its Nov. 23 14:37 UTC market snapshot.

The bars compare two dated observations.

The November contract accounted for $5.75 million, while the December contract attracted another $5.62 million. The remaining volume came from contracts covering March and December 2027.

The sharp repricing illustrates how strongly traders had discounted Huang's prospects of returning before the end of November, only for NVIDIA's board to reverse its earlier decision.

Under Polymarket's resolution rules, Huang needed to return to NVIDIA in a formal executive, advisory, or governance capacity before the relevant deadline.

His reinstatement as both chief executive and director satisfies those conditions, turning what had been considered an unlikely outcome into a confirmed corporate development.

This means Stellar continues to grow in tokenized assets, a major highlight of strong growth in Q3, 2026.

Sources indicate that real-world assets tokenized on Stellar amounted to $4.1 billion at the end of Q3 2026, up 36% from Q2 and up 548% from Q3 2025. Two assets drove the bulk of the quarter’s growth: Tradable’s fresh tokenized private credit and continued inflows into the Spiko Amundi overnight swap fund.

It has been revealed that in late August 2026, Stellar held more tokenized non-US government debt than any other blockchain, with about $490 million in sovereign instruments. These included Spiko’s euro Treasury bill fund, Mexican CETES and Brazilian Tesouro bonds through Etherfuse, South Korean Treasury bonds, and a Marshall Islands digital sovereign bond.

Stellar has widened access to tokenized funds in the United States, Europe and Asia. Franklin Templeton’s BENJI has been on Stellar since 2021. In August 2026, the SEC's Division of Investment Management issued a no-action letter confirming that the Franklin Templeton's registered mutual funds and ETFs may use BENJI for cash management. This expands the set of institutions permitted to hold it. Franklin Templeton made a similar move in Europe, registering 'grBenji' as a Luxembourg UCITS share class for third-party distribution, now live on 21X.

In a recent development, in Asia, Marketnode unveiled in August that it will offer funds from BNY Investments on Stellar, with Marketnode acting as the tokenization and distribution platform. Together, these developments expand access to tokenized funds on Stellar for institutions in the United States, Europe and Asia.

State Street Investment Management and Galaxy brought their Onchain Liquidity Sweep Fund to Stellar in September 2026.

Latest Update: Robinhood Chain pays Ethereum 70% more than Base despite collecting 64% less in fees

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robinhood Chain paid Ethereum 70% more than Coinbase-backed Base to settle transactions, even though it collected 64% fewer user fees over 30 days.
  • The network spent approximately $25,700 on Ethereum settlement costs between Oct.
  • However, Base generated $2.97 million in transaction fees over the same period, nearly three times Robinhood Chain's $1.07 million.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robinhood Chain paid Ethereum 70% more than Coinbase-backed Base to settle transactions, even though it collected 64% fewer user fees over 30 days.

The network spent approximately $25,700 on Ethereum settlement costs between Oct. 23 and Nov. 21, compared with Base's $15,100, according to Castle Labs data compiled from growthepie.

However, Base generated $2.97 million in transaction fees over the same period, nearly three times Robinhood Chain's $1.07 million.

That disparity left Robinhood Chain spending $2.41 on Ethereum settlement for every $100 collected from consumers, compared with just 51 cents for Base.

The figures expose a significant difference in the networks' settlement costs, even as both retain the overwhelming majority of transaction fees after paying Ethereum.

The gap is particularly striking because Base consumed considerably more Ethereum data capacity.

According to Blobscan data, Base posted approximately 350,000 blobs during the period, nearly twice Robinhood Chain's 182,000. Blobs let Ethereum's layer-2 networks publish transaction data at lower cost.

Base consequently spent about $4,478 on blob fees, compared with Robinhood Chain's $2,315.

However, the remaining settlement costs tell a different story. Excluding blob fees, Robinhood Chain spent approximately $23,379, more than double Base's $10,602.

Those additional expenses include standard Ethereum transaction fees for posting data and updating settlement states.

According to recent reports, settlement and data-posting costs in USD. Labels show the UTC start dates of four seven-day periods in 2026. The article covers Nov. 20 and 21 separately.

Source: growthepie Robinhood Chain daily settlement fees · growthepie Base daily settlement fees.

The comparison highlights a broader imbalance in Ethereum's scaling economy, where layer-2 networks collect transaction fees while paying relatively little to the blockchain securing their operations.

It has been revealed that across all tracked Ethereum layer-2 networks, people paid approximately $5 million in fees during the 30 days ending Nov. 21, while the networks paid Ethereum just $74,500 for settlement and data availability.

That represents roughly 1.5% of user fees, leaving approximately 98.5% after Ethereum settlement expenses, before accounting for other operating and revenue-sharing costs.

Base and Robinhood Chain accounted for about $4.04 million of those combined fees but paid Ethereum only $40,800.

The difference reflects how Ethereum's scaling architecture distributes economic activity. Layer-2 networks handle user transactions and collect their associated fees, while Ethereum provides settlement and data availability for a comparatively small charge.

For Ethereum, the resulting payments contribute to transaction fee burning and validator income, but remain modest relative to the economic activity taking place on its scaling networks.

The November figures raise two questions: whether Robinhood Chain can narrow its settlement-cost disadvantage against Base, and how much additional revenue Ethereum can capture as layer-2 networks continue handling most user activity.

The past weeks have seen the broad crypto ETF market face consistent withdrawals from investors, causing Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, and others to record steady outflows since October.

While the negative trend has continued, Solana has just taken over the leadership in the broad ETF market after recording its first inflow in a while.

Latest data from SosoValue reveals that while Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP ETFs have continued to struggle with consistent weekly outflows, Solana has just beaten the trend after it finally ended a six-week streak of consecutive weekly outflows.

Notably, the data indicates that Solana spot ETFs have recorded a net inflow of $4.38 million over the week.

Although the net amount of capital received by the ETFs appears decent, it is significant considering the growing crypto market weakness.

While this marks an end to the Solana ETFs' six-week outflow streak, this is the first positive weekly performance they have recorded since October 9.

Further data demonstrates that Bitcoin spot ETFs suffered the largest withdrawals as investors pulled out about $1.79 billion during the same period.

The negative trend also extended to the Ethereum ETF market as the funds posted a total of $314.17 million in net outflows following the consistent selling pressure.

In addition to this, the XRP spot ETFs were not spared, as the funds recorded $11.11 million in weekly outflows, leaving Solana as the only one among the four major crypto ETFs to finish the week on a positive note.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP ETF Shares Surface in Schwab’s Repo Collateral.

XRP ETF shares just appeared in collateral baskets pledged by JPMorgan & Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund.

XRP exchange-traded fund shares appeared in collateral baskets posted by JPMorgan and Bank of America to a Schwab money market fund, according to wealth coach Kamilah Stevenson.

In her latest YouTube episode, she argues that the reported holdings point to a less visible source of institutional demand: securities pledged against loans rather than bought for price exposure.

In a recent development, the distinction matters. Stevenson states Schwab did not buy XRP or the ETFs outright; its fund lent cash and received baskets of securities backing the transactions.

Citing monthly SEC disclosures, Stevenson identifies XRP ETF shares from Grayscale, Canary, Franklin and Bitwise among collateral supplied by the banks’ trading arms.

She puts their combined value at roughly $36,000 in April, $2 million in June and more than $8 million by August, an increase exceeding 200-fold.

In a recent development, those figures remain claims presented in the video. The transcript does not specify the reporting year or filing identifiers, limiting verification of the sequence.

Stevenson acknowledges that the positions were small relative to the underlying loans. Their inclusion would demonstrate acceptance of particular ETF securities within collateral baskets, not necessarily an institutional commitment to holding XRP directly.

According to recent reports, the YouTube video episode connects those reported positions to BlackRock’s effort to expand acceptance of tokenized fund shares as collateral. Dr. Stevenson says the appeal is straightforward: investors could pledge income-producing fund shares instead of redeeming them to provide cash.

She also points to Binance’s acceptance of BlackRock’s BUIDL fund as collateral and describes a wider shift toward blockchain-based collateral transfers. Her thesis is that assets used to secure financing can generate more persistent demand than assets held solely for trading.

“Trading creates excitement; collateral creates demand that stays,” Dr. Stevenson claims.

That argument needs a boundary. Acceptance of XRP ETF shares does not establish that lenders accept XRP itself, and tokenized collateral does not automatically require XRP to move between markets. Stevenson presents direct XRP-backed lending and cross-currency settlement as potential next steps, not completed developments.

Veteran trader Peter Brandt has softened the tone of his recent Bitcoin warnings and noted on X that the cryptocurrency held at the level it needed to hold after its drop to $55,150 over the weekend.

"Bitcoin held exactly where it had to hold -- for now anyway, but perhaps for more than now," Brandt wrote on Monday.

Sources indicate that brandt also shared a monthly chart of Bitcoin together with the post. The chart goes back to 2018, and Brandt marked on it the same patterns that he had already pointed to in previous years. According to the chart, the price of Bitcoin was back above $63,000 at the time of the post and stood at $63,338.

On Saturday, Bitcoin fell as low as $55,150. It was the lowest price of the cryptocurrency since September 2024, and before that, the lowest price of Bitcoin in 2026 was $57,718 on July 1, according to Coinbase.

Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 15, Brandt posted a weekly chart with a possible head-and-shoulders top and mentioned that, if the pattern proves valid, Bitcoin's October 2025 record of about $126,000 may not be surpassed in his lifetime. Two days before that, on Nov. 13, Bitcoin dropped below $70,000 for the first time since August.

Brandt has also pointed to the history of Bitcoin's bull market cycles more than once. Late last year, he posted a chart showing that each of Bitcoin's five major bull runs began after drawdowns of 75% or more, and he wrote that if the decline carried to $50,000, "the next bull market cycle should carry to $200k to $250K.".

In April, Brandt remarked that Bitcoin could form an "investable low" in September or October 2026. According to Brandt, this low may or may not go below the February low near $60,000, and the next cycle peak could land between $300,000 and $500,000 in September or October 2029 if the four-year cycle continues to hold.

"Real bottom will not occur until October 2026," Brandt mentioned in an interview in February.

The latest Brandt post comes amid a rally in U.S. tech stocks on Monday. Earlier that day, Nvidia unveiled that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive officer and board member, effective immediately.

According to recent reports, according to the Nvidia announcement, the board received input from senior levels of the U.S. government before the decision, and it is confident that Huang's return "poses no national security risk." Shares of Nvidia surged 33% after the news, according to CNBC.

Sources indicate that bitcoin went up together with tech stocks and briefly climbed above $64,000 on Monday. Before the Nvidia news, Bitcoin had already recovered from the Saturday low to around $61,500.

Huang resigned from Nvidia on Nov. 12. On Nov. 17, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones mentioned on the firm's earnings call that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, monad is preparing to unlock 16.61 billion MON tokens on Nov. 24, exceeding its circulating supply as the cryptocurrency hits record lows.

The release represents 140.5% of the 11.83 billion MON right now circulating and marks the first major insider distribution since the blockchain debuted in November 2025.

According to DefiLlama, approximately 10.7 billion MON will go to team members, 4.925 billion to investors, and 987.5 million to the Category Labs treasury. This means its team and investor allocations account for 94% of the release.

The unlock was valued at approximately $226 million in Tokenomist's earlier estimate, but MON's decline has reduced its value to roughly $190 million, still exceeding the token's $137 million market capitalization.

CryptoSlate's data demonstrates MON plunged around 11% over the past 24 hours, touching an all-time low of $0.01152 ahead of the release. It is trading at $0.012 as of press time.

The incoming supply adds to existing market pressure, with further insider distributions scheduled through 2029.

Historical data from Alea Research highlights that 16 comparable token unlocks recorded median declines of 25.2% in the preceding month and 6.9% in the following month.

Category Labs has authorized up to $80 million in MON repurchases through Dec. 31, although Alea found no disclosed purchases under the program.

Beyond potential selling, the release could alter how Monad distributes voting power and staking rewards.

Industry observers note that the network had 20.73 billion MON backing validator votes across 197 operators on Nov. 22, according to Valopers.

If insiders stake just 2.3 billion MON, approximately 14% of their newly available allocation, those tokens would account for 10% of the resulting voting power, assuming existing stake remains unchanged.

At 25% participation, approximately 4.15 billion MON would enter active staking, representing 16.7% of the expanded total.

That scenario would also reduce gross inflationary rewards per staked MON by 16.7%, assuming issuance and validator commissions remain constant.

Three scenarios model additions to active stake from the estimated 16.613 billion MON release scheduled for November 24.

If a quarter of the estimated release enters active stake, the upcoming MON would represent 16.7% of the enlarged total.

All three scenarios assume the displayed amounts become active stake and the existing stake stays fixed. They model aggregate voting weight after activation. Actual delegations and recipient validators can vary.

Amounts are rounded to two decimals and shares to one.

Sources indicate that all three scenarios assume the displayed amounts become active stake and the existing stake stays fixed. They model aggregate voting weight after activation. Actual delegations and recipient validators can vary.

The potential redistribution comes amid substantial concentration of Foundation-linked staking allocations.

Alea estimated that Foundation-linked wallets accounted for 78% of active stake on Nov. 1, while Backpack controlled 10.82% of validator voting weight on Nov. 22.

Industry observers note that monad initially prohibited staking locked insider tokens to direct more early rewards toward public holders. The restriction expires with the unlock, allowing newly eligible tokens to compete for staking rewards and validator influence.

The first post-unlock delegations will show whether insiders reinforce the largest validators or spread voting power across smaller operators, while trading activity will reveal how much of the newly introduced supply reaches exchanges.

Industry observers note that last week, Bitcoin [BTC] fell to a low of $55,130 on Saturday, the 20th of November. This was lower than $57,800, which the leading crypto registered on the 1st of July.

It led to debate around whether the bear market was truly over, or whether what we saw in August-September was only a pause within the longer-term bearish trend.

Over the past two weeks, Bitcoin liquidations exceeded $600 million on four separate days.

The 11th and the 20th of November, when BTC breached key support levels at $73k and $61.4k, saw the heaviest long liquidations. Also, contextually speaking, these two days witnessed $690 million and $670 million in long liquidations, respectively.

The persistent downward price action was accompanied by relentless selling. Since the 5th of November, every trading day bar one has seen negative spot ETF flows.

Last week’s net outflows alone reached $1.245 billion. This incessant selling would need to ease before Bitcoin could find room to recover.

In a recent development, as things stand, a weekly trading session close below $57,800 is needed to flip the structure bearishly. The previous week’s correction, though deep, might be just a liquidity sweep before a recovery.

Bitcoin holders are under severe strain as prices approach or drop below their cost basis, and Open Interest has plunged dramatically. It was a result of tightening monetary policy and the global equity market downturn.

Over the past year, the BTC Open Interest was down by $4.5 billion.

In a recent development, in July, this figure fell as low as $6.5 billion. It was the largest OI downturn in Bitcoin’s history in dollar terms, observed crypto analyst Darkfost.

It has been revealed that there have been eight trading days in 2026 with over $1.5 billion in liquidations across the crypto market. A decline in risk appetite among investors, several liquidation cascades, and the overarching bearish price action for most of the year helped explain the OI drop.

A leverage reset can be healthy for the market.

According to recent reports, alongside the weekly BTC chart, there was hope for a bear market bottom. Even so, it remains risky to buy, as a bear market continuation cannot yet be fully ruled out.

An Anthropic mathematician says Claude helped him crack the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old puzzle with a $1 million prize attached.

His claim surfaced Friday, one day after the AI organization’s stock-market debut, and has not yet been independently verified.

“I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis,” Levent Alpöge wrote in a four-page note. He indicates the method also resolves the broader Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, which extends the question to other mathematical functions.

You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Anthropic with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.

In a recent development, alpöge indicates he and Claude encoded their argument in Lean, software used to check mathematical proofs step by step. His note links to 14 downloadable parts of the proof archive, but its availability does not amount to acceptance by the mathematical community.

Alpöge states he messaged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei about a possible announcement “late Sunday night,” November 15. He then consulted firm leadership and remarked there was a constraint to respect, without explaining precisely what it was.

According to recent reports, “The precise timing is horrible,” he acknowledged. Alpöge rejected a cynical interpretation of the timing, but did not explicitly say the tech giant’s IPO caused the delay.

Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq Thursday, November 19, after raising $81.34 billion in its offering.

Alpöge figured in September’s AI math wars. OpenAI claimed it had solved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem as he and NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster pursued related fluid-equation work, sparking a credit dispute over research priority.

Industry observers note that openAI followed in October with 722 manuscripts generated by an unreleased model, grouped into 372 families of results. Only 162 included Lean-checked main results, and mathematicians demanded stronger evidence rather than accepting the tech giant’s flood of claims at face value.

Recent findings suggest that some mathematicians fear a “mathocalypse,” with AI solving coveted problems before researchers can learn from pursuing them. Toronto mathematician Daniel Litt warned that, without adaptation, “there’s just no more math in 50 years.” At an MIT panel this week, Buckmaster argued mathematics still requires human understanding.

Recent findings suggest that first posed by Bernhard Riemann in 1859, the hypothesis predicts where certain zeros of the Riemann zeta function fall. The question matters because those zeros are linked to the distribution of prime numbers, whose patterns underlie extensive mathematical research.

A proof would be a historic mathematical result, since experts have been trying to solve that for over a century.

Industry observers note that lean can verify that formal deductions obey its rules. Mathematicians still need to reproduce the archive, check the formalized theorem matches the original conjecture, and examine the claimed result before considering it settled.

Industry observers note that anthropic previously reported progress on the zeta function without claiming to solve the full hypothesis. Alpöge’s new assertion goes far beyond that earlier work.

In a recent development, the Clay Mathematics Institute lists the Riemann hypothesis among its Millennium Prize Problems, each carrying a $1 million award. Under the institute’s prize rules, a proposed solution must be published in a qualifying outlet, survive at least two years of scrutiny, and earn general acceptance before the prize can be considered.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite the sharp fall in the cryptocurrency market, Michael Saylor-led Strategy has not stopped its Bitcoin (BTC) buying spree, as it picked up 457 BTC worth around $29.6 million.

The firm's recent purchase comes as the leading cryptocurrency has been struggling to rebound from the heavy sell-off that recently dragged it to a two-plus-year low.

The latest data from Strategy's SEC filing reveals that the firm has bought 457 Bitcoin at an average price of $64,898 per coin.

The new purchase brings Strategy’s Bitcoin holdings to around 851,305 BTC, which accounts for over 4% of the cryptocurrency's maximum supply of 21 million coins.

The firm has now spent around $64.23 billion to build its Bitcoin holdings at an average price of $75,446 per Bitcoin.

It is worth noting that Strategy has been buying BTC at gradually decreasing prices as the cryptocurrency market continues to bleed heavily.

According to recent reports, on Nov. 2, the firm declared that it had bought 811 BTC, worth around $65.5 million, at an average price of $80,846 per Bitcoin.

A week later, on Nov. 9, Strategy unveiled the purchase of 1,036 BTC worth $81.9 million at an average price of $79,012.

The firm’s Bitcoin purchase a week later, on Nov. 16, was relatively smaller at 485 BTC, worth $33.4 million, with an average price of $68,887.

Sources indicate that the latest 457 BTC purchase continues this pattern. The latest Strategy purchase was made at an almost 20% lower price than the firm’s Nov. 2 acquisition.

Overall, the firm has made four weekly purchases, scooping up around 2,789 BTC worth $210.4 million.

Sources indicate that however, these purchases have been much smaller than before. The latest $29.6 million purchase is almost 64% lower than the $81.9 million purchase declared just two weeks ago.

Although Saylor is doubling down on Bitcoin, Strategy’s massive holdings in the cryptocurrency are underwater as the market has been struggling to regain its footing.

Industry observers note that on Nov. 21, Bitcoin hit a low of around $55,130, its lowest level since September 2024, before rebounding above $61,000.

The firm’s recent purchases have helped reduce its overall average Bitcoin acquisition cost, but the drop has not been that significant.

For example, with the latest purchase, the average cost of the firm’s Bitcoin holdings dropped from $75,452 to around $75,446, a decline of just $6 per Bitcoin.

At the same time, the firm has also been putting a lot of resources into supporting its preferred securities.

In the latest reporting period, Strategy sold around 1.93 million common shares, raising net proceeds of $176.7 million.

It has been revealed that is THIS dip a good time to invest? One analyst thinks so.

Bitcoin’s Fear & Greed Index stood at 11, compared to 50 in early November, reflecting a sharp shift in market sentiment alongside BTC’s 20% correction. Long-term investors may benefit from this as many weak holders are offloading their BTC. This allows large investors to take up the BTC on sale, allowing them to buy it cheaper.

Against this backdrop, Michael Saylor’s recent post showing his famous Bitcoin buying signal suggests whales may be getting into the market.

With BTC falling toward $56k, extreme fear, and Strategy’s continued purchases, it does lend some support to the analyst’s view that this dip could be a buying opportunity.

But the bigger question remains: Does buying the dip offer enough long-term upside?

Recent findings suggest that in terms of on-chain and technical indicators, BTC has seen a 40% pullback from its post-election rally in 2024. From a long-term perspective, it has also pulled back to levels seen 5 years prior.

This means Bitcoin has erased years of price gains, raising questions about whether the recent correction can be viewed as a buying opportunity or if it is indicative of a deeper market downturn.

According to recent reports, simply put, does Bitcoin’s long-term return profile justify Michael Saylor’s latest purchase and analysts’ bullish outlook? Or could weakening returns and a prolonged price decline discourage smart money from accumulating Bitcoin [BTC]?

Key onchain signals are already showing a divergence from the analysts’ bullish outlook.

While there is extreme fear in the market, a whale moved 2,279 BTC into Binance, while another whale took a 40x BTC short worth $91 million.

It has been revealed that extreme fear has historically attracted bargain hunters. However, these whale transactions suggested some large investors were preparing for further downside.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Bitcoin’s supply distribution painted an equally concerning picture. Nearly 57% of BTC’s supply was sitting at a loss, leaving just 43% in profit.

However, large players are taking a more risk-averse stance, making the possibility of further capitulation harder to ignore.

Sources indicate that ultimately, extreme fear alone may not be enough to confirm a bottom. This puts Saylor’s latest Bitcoin buy signal in a different light.

With BTC’s long-term structure weakening, limited signs of whale accumulation, and capitulation risks rising, buying the dip may carry more downside risk than potential upside.

Extreme fear and Strategy’s continued Bitcoin purchases suggest a potential buying opportunity, but they do not confirm a market bottom.

Rising supply in loss, whale selling, and large short positions point to further downside and capitulation risks.

Strategy raises its buyback ceiling to $4 billion as MSTR shares sink 21%

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1027 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cryptoslate

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Strategy raised its STRC buyback authorization for the third time on Monday, bringing the program to $4 billion as its common shares continued to struggle.
  • Sources indicate that the Bitcoin treasury company had exhausted nearly $2.88 billion, or nearly 96% of its previous $3 billion authorization, after spending another $211.8 million repurchasing STRC during the week ended Nov.
  • The latest expansion comes as Strategy's common shares have fallen 21.1% since it announced its first STRC repurchases on July 27.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Strategy raised its STRC buyback authorization for the third time on Monday, bringing the program to $4 billion as its common shares continued to struggle.

Sources indicate that the Bitcoin treasury company had exhausted nearly $2.88 billion, or nearly 96% of its previous $3 billion authorization, after spending another $211.8 million repurchasing STRC during the week ended Nov. 22.

The latest expansion comes as Strategy's common shares have fallen 21.1% since it announced its first STRC repurchases on July 27. MSTR closed at $77.80 on Nov. 20, compared with $98.65 nearly four months earlier.

Industry observers note that strategy debuted its initial $1 billion digital credit repurchase program in June, then increased it to $2 billion in September and $3 billion in October. Monday's announcement marks the third consecutive $1 billion expansion, bringing cumulative expansion to $4 billion.

The growing commitment has coincided with a shift in how Strategy deploys money raised from common shareholders.

According to its latest SEC filing, the manufacturer issued 1.93 million MSTR shares last week, raising $176.7 million.

Of those proceeds, $147 million (83.2%) funded STRC repurchases, while only $29.6 million (16.8%) went toward acquiring 457 Bitcoin.

Strategy contributed another $64.8 million from existing cash to complete the $211.8 million preferred-share repurchase.

Weekly repurchase spending in US dollars, reported amounts are rounded to $0.1M.

Source: Strategy Form 8-K, Nov. 23, 2026 · STRC Live historical buyback ledger.

The spending has helped reduce its future dividend obligations but has not kept STRC consistently near its $100 stated amount. The security closed at $93.60 on Nov. 20, despite Strategy maintaining a 12% annual dividend rate to support its price.

Meanwhile, Strategy retains a separate $1 billion authorization to repurchase MSTR shares, which remained entirely unused last week.

Bitcoin analyst Derin Olenik criticized the continued issuance of common shares to finance preferred-share repurchases, arguing the transactions weaken shareholders' underlying Bitcoin exposure.

Strategy's published figures support a decline in gross Bitcoin holdings per assumed diluted share during the latest reporting week.

Sources indicate that its outstanding Bitcoin balance increased from 850,849 BTC on Nov. 15 to 851,305 BTC on Nov. 22, while assumed diluted shares outstanding rose from approximately 457.24 million to 459.19 million.

Consequently, gross Bitcoin per share declined from approximately 186,082 satoshis to 185,392 satoshis, a reduction of about 690 satoshis (0.37%).

However, Strategy executive chairman Michael Saylor defended the transactions, arguing that Strategy's approach has consistently increased shareholders' net Bitcoin exposure despite the dilution.

According to recent reports, “Our trades accreted Net BPS in each of the last 13 weeks. Cumulatively, we increased Net BPS by 584 sats/share and generated a Net BTC Gain of 2,505 BTC or $199M before preferred dividends, measured at a fixed $BTC price each week.”.

According to recent reports, strategy-reported positive weekly contributions to net BTC per common share (in satoshis) before preferred dividends and holding BTC price fixed within each week. Values are transcribed from the supplied Strategy-branded Nov. 23 chart at one-decimal precision.

Source: Strategy net BPS methodology; individual values from supplied Strategy-branded chart · Strategy, November 23, 2026 corporate disclosure · Strategy, November 19 commentary on previous 12 weeks.

Saylor also reported that the latest week's transactions increased Net Bitcoin Per Share by six satoshis and improved Strategy's Net Reserve by $183 million.

The conflicting figures reflect competing assessments of Strategy's capital allocation. Gross Bitcoin per share measures its holdings against diluted shares, while Strategy's Net Bitcoin Per Share accounts for senior claims and dollar assets when calculating the Bitcoin exposure attributable to common shareholders.

Under Saylor's framework, retiring preferred securities can increase net exposure even when common-share issuance reduces gross Bitcoin holdings per share.

Olenik remained critical of the economics, questioning whether the increasingly complex transactions justify the continued dilution of common shareholders.

According to recent reports, he also challenged the economics of STRC repurchases. His calculations put the security's average issuance price at $95.81 and its average repurchase price at $97.93, meaning Strategy has spent more buying back preferred shares than it originally received per share issued.

Average price estimated by dividing reported weekly spending, rounded to $0.1M, by shares repurchased. Per-share cents are approximate.

Sources indicate that source: Strategy Form 8-K, Nov. 23, 2026 · STRC Live historical buyback ledger.

Strategy has defended repurchases below STRC's $100 stated amount because retiring the securities reduces future dividend obligations.

Saylor said Strategy has reduced outstanding credit by $2.9 billion in recent months, lowering annual dividend obligations by approximately $353 million.

The latest transactions alone retired 2.18 million STRC shares, eliminating approximately $26.2 million in annualized dividends at the current 12% rate.

However, the company's latest decision suggests that reducing those obligations will remain a major capital priority.

Alongside the third buyback expansion, Strategy authorized transferring $1 billion from its dedicated USD Reserve into discretionary USD Cash, which management can use for further repurchases or Bitcoin purchases.

The change marks a departure from its original July policy, which explicitly prohibited using the USD Reserve to fund STRC repurchases.

Saylor remarked the reallocation was possible because the organization's remaining reserve could cover its dividend and interest obligations for 3.4 years.

Following the adjustment, Strategy reported approximately $3.7 billion in dedicated reserves and over $1 billion in discretionary cash, leaving total dollar assets at roughly $4.8 billion.

Olenik interpreted the move as evidence that Strategy was preparing to rely more heavily on existing liquidity when issuing MSTR shares becomes less attractive.

That would let Strategy continue retiring preferred securities without relying entirely on upcoming common-share issuance, although the company has not committed the reallocated cash to a specific purchase.

Strategy now has $1.1 billion in remaining preferred-share buyback authority, nearly matching its discretionary cash balance.

Its next capital-allocation decision will determine whether the expanded financial resources support further STRC repurchases or reverse the recent pattern of relatively modest Bitcoin purchases and continued MSTR dilution.

Notably, Bitcoin [BTC] climbed 3.56%, trading at $61,123 at the time of writing, but Midnight [NIGHT] took the cake as it had a considerably stronger run, gaining 13.25%.

While the wider market recovery may have helped NIGHT, the token’s 13.25% gain suggests a more isolated type of buying interest. Whether the token is able to maintain this surge and potentially break $0.053 really depends on buyers’ continued demand and how well Bitcoin holds its recent recovery.

In a recent development, NIGHT crypto has reclaimed the 23.6% Fibonacci level after briefly losing it on the 17th of November. At the time of writing, the token traded at $0.05.

Recent findings suggest that the token has largely traded within a $0.035-$0.053 range since October, suggesting an established consolidation in which buyers have repeatedly defended lower prices. This range has also limited upward advances, with the $0.053 area acting as a ceiling for the past two months.

The latest recovery has brought NIGHT towards its upper boundary once again. If the move above this range is sustained, it could signal a shift in market structure and open the door to further gains.

The RSI has recovered to 62.09, hinting at strengthening bullish momentum, and the OBV’s recent uptrend suggests that buying volume is supporting the token’s recovery.

In a recent development, looking at the H4 chart, NIGHT fell to $0.03896 on November 21 but made a quick recovery over the following two days. It has since reclaimed the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement at $0.04863, recovering most of its previous decline, bringing its previous swing high back into focus.

Recent findings suggest that the shift in momentum is also reflecting on the MACD as its moved above both its signal and zero lines. Furthermore, the OBV continued its upward trend, suggesting that buyers are slowly starting to re-enter the market, helping sustain the move higher.

NIGHT is now approaching its previous H4 swing high at $0.05126. Breaking above this level gives the bulls another shot at pushing out of the token’s two-month consolidation as it puts the daily range resistance at $0.05315 within reach.

However, another rejection would send NIGHT lower, with the daily 50% Fibonacci level at $0.03795 becoming the next support.

According to recent reports, on Monday, XRP briefly rose above $1 after the return of Jensen Huang to Nvidia sparked a rally on Wall Street and a wave of short liquidations in the crypto market. At the peak of the move, short liquidations on XRP exceeded long liquidations by 578%, according to CoinGlass data.

On the XRPUSDT perpetual contract on Binance, the price of XRP went from $0.94 to as high as $1.02 within minutes after 14:00 UTC, and later it pulled back and stood at $0.984, according to TradingView.

Earlier on Monday, before the opening bell, Nvidia announced that its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. The organization noted that the board was satisfied with Huang's "candor and ability to lead" after a series of meetings with him, and that its independent investigation would continue. According to the company, the board received input from senior U.S. government officials and concluded that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk.".

"The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones said in a statement.

Industry observers note that huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 12, and on Nov. 17, during the tech giant's earnings call, Jones said that the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

In premarket trading, Nvidia stock jumped 27% to $159.48 as of 9 a.m. ET, and at the start of U.S. trading on Monday, Nvidia shares were up more than 30%. The rally spread across Wall Street, and the S&P 500 rose as much as 5.6% and the Nasdaq 100 as much as 7.9%, according to NBC News.

Recent findings suggest that coinGlass data shows that $9.45 million worth of XRP positions were liquidated over the past 24 hours, and $7.18 million of that amount came from short positions. Long positions accounted for $2.27 million.

Industry observers note that the same happened across the rest of the crypto market. In total, 110,663 traders were liquidated for $660.89 million over the past 24 hours, according to CoinGlass, and shorts accounted for $515.94 million of that amount.

Sources indicate that bitcoin led the list with $273.26 million in liquidations, and 82.8% of that amount came from short positions. Ethereum followed with $139.07 million, and Solana was third with $24.93 million.

Besides, perpetual contracts on Nvidia stock and on SOXL, a triple-leveraged exchange-traded fund on semiconductor stocks, were next on the list with $16.34 million and $15.01 million in liquidations, respectively, according to CoinGlass.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

U.S. President Donald Trump wrapped up his third exclusive dinner for his biggest Official Trump [TRUMP] memecoin holders on the 22nd of November.

Hosted at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, the dinner offered access to the President and other prominent personalities to investors who held significant amounts of $TRUMP.

The top 185 holders qualified for the dinner, while the top 29 received invitations to a separate VIP reception. In fact, the top four were also promised an 18-karat gold Trump watch. This came after the November midterm elections, where Democrats swept the majority in both the House and Senate.

But this dinner is raising eyebrows like never before.

According to recent reports, this is because there was a sharp decline in participation. During the first $TRUMP memecoin gala in May 2025, eligible investors reportedly needed to hold at least $55,000 worth of tokens to qualify.

This time, one participant reportedly secured entry with just $518 worth of tokens.

Furthermore, more than 5,000 holders who could potentially have qualified did not even register, despite organizers extending the registration deadline by four days.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

More than 11,000 BTC moved from Coinbase and Binance to Kraken during Saturday's selloff, complicating Bitcoin's supply-squeeze narrative.

The five transactions, identified by Ask The Tape (ATT), came as major exchanges recorded hundreds of millions of dollars in net Bitcoin withdrawals, fueling expectations that fewer coins were available for trading.

However, the transfers revealed substantial movements between trading venues, with Bitcoin leaving some exchanges only to replenish reserves elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that coinbase accounted for approximately 4,028 BTC across two transactions. The first delivered 2,177.79 BTC to Kraken-tagged addresses at 03:47 UTC, followed by another 1,850 BTC at 10:04 UTC.

Binance then transferred 7,000 BTC through three transactions: two transfers of 2,000 BTC each and a third involving 3,000 BTC.

Sources indicate that nov. 21, 2026 UTC. The bands follow BTC from wallets tagged to Coinbase and Binance into Kraken-tagged wallets.

Withdrawals at the sending venues became gross receipts at another tracked exchange.

Industry observers note that the five transactions are a sample of Nov. 21 UTC activity. ATT supplies wallet-cluster labels. Beneficial ownership, trades and full-day net flows remain outside the diagram’s scope.

The movements coincided with substantial differences in exchange flows reported by CryptoQuant.

Recent findings suggest that binance recorded $680 million in net Bitcoin withdrawals on Nov. 21, while Coinbase and Bybit registered $373 million and $103 million, respectively. Together, the three exchanges lost approximately $1.16 billion.

Kraken moved in the opposite direction, receiving $478 million in net inflows and offsetting 41% of those withdrawals.

That left the four platforms with a combined net outflow of $678 million, even as substantial amounts of Bitcoin circulated between their wallets.

Kraken also recorded significant outgoing transactions that day, including one involving approximately 4,028 BTC, illustrating the rapid movement of liquidity across exchanges during the downturn.

The exchange movements have become particularly significant as Bitcoin struggles to recover from its recent decline below $60,000.

Although declining exchange reserves can reduce the amount of Bitcoin immediately available for sale, sustained buying demand remains essential to turning that scarcity into upward price pressure.

That demand has weakened considerably among US institutional investors.

According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.7 billion in net withdrawals last week, extending a period of heavy redemptions that has stripped billions of dollars from the funds this month.

Sources indicate that while Bitcoin subsequently recovered above $61,000 on Nov. 23, the ETF withdrawals have yet to show a corresponding recovery in institutional appetite.

The next test arrives Wednesday, when the US Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes October's personal consumption expenditures inflation report alongside its second estimate of third-quarter economic growth.

According to recent reports, both releases are scheduled for 8:30 a.m. ET and could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's December interest rate decision.

Stronger inflation could push Treasury yields and the dollar higher, adding pressure to Bitcoin at a time when ETF investors are withdrawing capital.

That leaves Bitcoin's recovery dependent on two developments: exchange reserves continuing to decline across trading venues and fresh buying demand returning to absorb available supply.

If ETF withdrawals persist while Bitcoin continues circulating between exchanges, the apparent supply squeeze may offer little support against another wave of selling.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) has initiated a significant legal push to address the theft of over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance by North Korean hackers last month.
  • 23 announcement, the DOJ mentioned that it has filed a civil forfeiture complaint to recover over $1.1 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as part of its efforts to retrieve the billions lost in the massive hack.
  • The recent development comes less than a month after North Korean hackers reportedly broke into Binance on Oct.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States Department of Justice (DOJ) has initiated a significant legal push to address the theft of over $6 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance by North Korean hackers last month.

As per a Nov. 23 announcement, the DOJ mentioned that it has filed a civil forfeiture complaint to recover over $1.1 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as part of its efforts to retrieve the billions lost in the massive hack.

The recent development comes less than a month after North Korean hackers reportedly broke into Binance on Oct. 29 in one of the biggest crypto heists ever.

The DOJ claimed that its recent civil forfeiture action focuses on over $1.1 billion worth of USD Coin (USDC), a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar and issued by Circle.

The assets are alleged to have been stolen from Binance and laundered by North Korean cybercriminals.

Significantly, the assets had previously been frozen under a restraining order obtained by the government earlier this month. With the fresh court filing, the potential recovery of the assets has taken another step forward.

In a recent development, the DOJ further claimed that U.S. authorities have successfully helped freeze, seize or return over $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency since the attack in October.

This is nearly half of the total $6 billion-plus stolen from Binance, though the government did not provide details about how much of that has been returned to the exchange.

Recent findings suggest that the importance of collaboration between law enforcement agencies and crypto firms to ensure that hackers don't get away with stolen assets was stressed by Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva.

Recent findings suggest that “North Korean cyber hackers stole over $6 billion of cryptocurrency from Binance. But prompt coordination with both the government and our private sector partners helped to avoid the bulk of these assets from being lost,” Duva said.

Recent findings suggest that U.S. authorities have further revealed the sophisticated money laundering techniques used by North Korean hackers to conceal their stolen cryptocurrency.

FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman remarked that the regime uses intricate money laundering methods to convert stolen digital assets into funds for its illicit activities.

After the Binance hack, authorities rapidly worked to trace the stolen funds and coordinate with crypto service providers to block further transfers.

In a recent development, the U.S. Secret Service claimed that its investigators were able to detect and freeze some of the stolen funds within minutes of the hack.

"The bad actors in this intrusion thought they could run from law enforcement. They've found out they were wrong," said Secret Service Special Agent in Charge Todd Bratz.

With the deeper correction in the cryptocurrency market, we are finally witnessing somewhat of a bounce in multiple top-15 digital assets, including XRP, Monero and Dogecoin.

XRP is printing higher network usage compared to October, Monero is gradually outperforming the market in the last 24 hours and Dogecoin is aiming at a local price recovery, even though a modest one.

According to recent reports, one notable development that we haven't anticipated is Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia (NVDA) CEO on November 23, only 11 days after his resignation. The announcement triggered a substantial market retrace, with NVDA stock gaining over 30% and Nasdaq adding around 6.8%, recovering a large share of last week's losses.

Thankfully, XRP highlights us resilience beyond regular market metrics: the average daily payments throughout the month have crossed the 1.1 million threshold, a 107% growth versus the October baseline. The basis behind the reversal is considerable: the rise in market volatility that triggered a substantial breakdown in the asset.

Industry observers note that with rapid market swings, it's no surprise that the asset saw more than 1.33 million transactions throughout the first 7 days of the month. Fresh accounts over a rolling 24-hour period reached 4,065 wallets, per XRPScan query on November 23.

From the technical standpoint, XRP is at the moment trading near the $0.99 price level, approximately 23% lower compared to the 30-day average, which fits the aforementioned bearish narrative. The decline in spot trading volume is also an important sign: spot investors dropped around 22.5% of their trading activities throughout the month.

The drop in futures volume also makes the picture slightly more complicated than it should be. Following the price breakdown, the volatility increase was followed by an increase in open interest, so the drop we're witnessing right now is more of a return to the baseline than an matter on its own.

It has been revealed that the current price resistance and support points are quite diverse, but not thoroughly tested, apart from a local support level at $0.9. The immediate breakout test is going to take place at approximately $0.99, with a possibility of a further recovery. The level at $1.00 is more of a psychological barrier, while $1.04 is the threshold that should mark the end of the downtrend.

In a recent development, according to CoinMarketCap's data, Monero has been steadily underperforming XRP and Dogecoin in the last 24 hours, though it's important to separate rising demand and active speculative buying. In the last 24 hours, Monero has gained over 4.7% in price. Futures open interest has crossed the $230 million mark.

Recent findings suggest that as already mentioned, Monero is a weaker performer out of the three, with a 4.7% gain over the last 24 hours. Unexpectedly, a deeper look reveals a set of issues: spot and futures volume, open interest and liquidation volume suggest a rather stale market with no momentum rather than an explosive recovery that might turn into a proper uptrend. The good news is that most of the liquidated volume is on the short side.

Sources indicate that from the network usage perspective, Monero is struggling, with its transaction count dropping below the 30-day average, prompting baseless price resilience. Though Monero's network design certainly limits the possibility of a thorough analysis due to its protected transaction design.

The most key development around Monero was, of course, the most recent Wrapped Monero incident. Despite the wrapped token itself having little to do with the main network of the asset, the coin itself had to withstand the rippling selling pressure. The token lost more than 99% of its value, causing $13 million in losses.

The main network itself went through a security audit on November 18, which found no high- or medium-severity vulnerabilities and only minor security complications, which developers have been notified about.

If the technical side of the question is rather important, the most important immediate price levels are the 508-510 range, which corresponds to the current breakout area, and the immediate support at $500.

Compared to all three cryptocurrencies, Monero is the only one showing some positivity over the last 7 days, despite the wrapped token incident. Privacy assets like XMR or Zcash quite often provide more market resilience during breakdowns, most likely due to the demand for privacy that always exists in the industry.

Dogecoin's technical recovery attempt is hitting somewhat of a wall, with daily, weekly and four-hour trends showing a clear bearish dynamic in addition to the price moving below all 8 tracked moving averages on the chart.

As the CoinGlass data suggests, the trading activity we are witnessing today is mixed: spot and futures volumes are descending, with a slight increase in open interest. $584 million in futures volume and $86 million in spot volume. Long and short liquidations are balanced.

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, the lack of network activity suggests a baseless price recovery on the market right now: only 37 thousand addresses were active in the last 24 hours, a 24% decrease YTD. Additionally, explorer data suggests that the ten largest DOGE addresses hold more than 44% of the token's available supply.

It doesn't suggest that only 10 users hold a large part of the token's supply, but rather a high concentration of DOGE on exchanges, which quite often prompts additional selling pressure.

It has been revealed that with the low volume and open interest, any technical price level, both resistance and support, can get invalidated swiftly; however, highlighting them could be useful. The first resistance rests at $0.0599, with a trend recovery threshold located around $0.06.

Support levels lie all the way down to the key psychological level of $0.05, the nearest being $0.054. The obvious trend reversal threshold is, of course, $0.06. Until the price establishes a foothold above it, discussing a recovery is not the best option out there.

In a recent development, across Al Zimmermann’s programming contests, METR reported median placements from the 96th to the 98th percentile for Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. About four people still beat the strongest models in the median contest.

The agents had 48 hours per contest on a 28-core machine. Each submission gave them a numerical score they could use to see whether their changes improved the result. Human contestants typically had about three calendar months, used their own hardware and could see the public standings. METR compared the agents’ scores with the original contest results.

Sources indicate that in a separate exercise, METR asked agents to design tests that would help researchers assess what AI models could do. AI judges and a human scorer had access to project files, scores from trial runs and the agents’ case for why their tests were relevant and feasible. The human scorer assessed whether each proposed test was worth including in METR’s suite. METR mentioned none of the designs was useful enough to include in its report.

The AI judges tended to agree more closely with the human scorer when a weaker model had designed the test. When the model that designed the test was as capable as the judge or stronger, the judges tended to rate the work more highly than the human did. Opus 5.5 agreed most closely with the human scorer, yet rated GPT-6 Astra’s proposals about 0.2 points higher on average on a scale from zero to one.

Sources indicate that the comparison came from one exercise, and what counted as useful depended in part on METR’s research priorities. METR said models underused some resources in the judgment tests. It also reported strong model performance on some longer machine-learning tasks with automatic scoring. A separate AI peer review audit tested whether reviewers’ objections changed the findings by running code on the underlying data.

METR replayed past coding contests and separately asked models to grade proposed AI evaluations.

In the judging exercise, a rating gap this large could change whether METR’s rubric called for more work on a proposed test.

It has been revealed that contest time and hardware differed between agents and humans. The judging gap reflects one exercise and METR’s own usefulness criteria.

According to recent reports, contest time and hardware differed between agents and humans. The judging gap reflects one exercise and METR’s own usefulness criteria.

Sources indicate that METR set score-and-time benchmarks for 34 of its 36 fresh tasks. It used direct human baselines for three and researcher estimates for the other 31.

METR remarked a gap that large could change whether the rubric recommended spending more time on a test.

  • It has been revealed that over the weekend, Bitcoin’s price on Kraken’s BTC/CAD trading pair suddenly dropped to C$24,250.
  • Sources indicate that this came as a shock because Bitcoin was trading around $57,650 on Kraken’s BTC/USD market during that period.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crypto exchange Kraken recently faced a flash crash that was caused by a liquidity shortage in one of its Canadian-dollar trading markets, rather than an actual crash in Bitcoin [BTC]’s global market price.

It has been revealed that over the weekend, Bitcoin’s price on Kraken’s BTC/CAD trading pair suddenly dropped to C$24,250. This was equivalent to approximately $16,900 at the prevailing USD/CAD exchange rate.

Sources indicate that this came as a shock because Bitcoin was trading around $57,650 on Kraken’s BTC/USD market during that period. In Bitcoin trading at nearly 70% below its price on other markets.

However, this was not a market-wide Bitcoin crash, as other major exchanges continued to show Bitcoin trading between $55,000 and $60,000.

The primary suspected reason was a sudden shortage of liquidity in Kraken’s BTC/CAD order book. This liquidity shortage, aka liquidity vacuum, is what caused a sudden price crash without Bitcoin’s actual market value declining.

Expressing their opinion on the matter, Blockstream CEO Adam Back suggested that the disruption may have originated from a market maker running out of funds in Kraken’s USD/CAD market.

As expected, this distortion may have spread to other CAD trading pairs through arbitrage, where traders buy assets at lower prices and sell them elsewhere at higher prices.

However, Kraken has not confirmed this explanation, yet. The exchange maintained that all orders were processed correctly and refused to reverse completed trades.

This followed the exchange experiencing a one-hour technical outage on 30 October 2026, affecting its website, app, and trading APIs.

But at the same time, Kraken recently expanded its xStocks platform to over 1,000 tokenized stock listings, according to AMBCrypto’s previous report.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A single Sentora vault supplied virtually all the Ripple USD (RLUSD) in Morpho’s Ethereum market for loans against wrapped XRP on Nov.
  • The market demonstrated about 7.1 million RLUSD in outstanding loans and 1 million RLUSD available for fresh loans.
  • Sentora’s lending decisions can change both how much credit is available and the interest rate on existing loans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A single Sentora vault supplied virtually all the Ripple USD (RLUSD) in Morpho’s Ethereum market for loans against wrapped XRP on Nov. 23.

The market demonstrated about 7.1 million RLUSD in outstanding loans and 1 million RLUSD available for fresh loans. Borrowers use FXRP, a token backed by XRP, to borrow the RLUSD stablecoin.

Sentora’s lending decisions can change both how much credit is available and the interest rate on existing loans.

At about 13:08 UTC, Morpho’s market dashboard put the Sentora RLUSD Main vault’s contribution at about 8.15 million RLUSD, or 99.99% of the market’s supply as displayed.

Borrowers had used 87.45% of the funds supplied to the market, a measure Morpho calls utilization, and the dashboard indicated a variable borrow rate of 4.99%.

Earlier on Nov. 23, one wallet posted 3,000 FXRP as collateral and borrowed 1,500 RLUSD in the same transaction, according to Morpho’s indexed activity.

Flare’s FXRP documentation describes FXRP as a tokenized representation of native XRP, and its FAssets system verifies XRP Ledger transactions used to mint FXRP and supports redemption for native XRP.

Flare’s August announcement describes how holders can mint FXRP on Flare, bridge it to Ethereum through the FAssets Portal or Stargate, and post it as collateral in this market. Anyone already holding the market’s FXRP on Ethereum can start at the collateral step.

In a recent development, A borrower’s position can be liquidated if its debt exceeds 77% of the collateral’s value, as measured by the market’s price feed. A drop in collateral value can push a borrower closer to that threshold even without taking out another loan.

In a separate Nov. 23 transaction, the market log indicates the Sentora vault withdrew 7,147.88 RLUSD. The vault’s allocation history shows the same transaction moving funds in two other lending markets, one backed by USDe and the other by syrupUSDC.

A later withdrawal of 10,498.74 RLUSD from the FXRP market appears in both logs.

The FXRP market made up just 2.41% of the funds allocated by the Sentora vault, which reported 338.36 million RLUSD in deposits and 95.27 million RLUSD in liquidity across the vault.

In October, the same market had about 8.53 million RLUSD from Sentora and a 10 million RLUSD allocation cap. By Nov. 23, the cap was 15 million RLUSD, while Sentora supplied about 8.15 million.

Recent findings suggest that the available funds for fresh borrowers were the 1 million RLUSD already in the market. Morpho’s liquidity API demonstrated zero additional RLUSD available at about 13:10 UTC through its Public Allocator, which can move funds from participating vaults when their settings permit it.

Other borrows or allocations can change the amount available before a transaction executes. That same reading highlighted that about 207,500 RLUSD of additional borrowing would bring the market to 90% utilization with supply unchanged.

Nov. 23 snapshot of Morpho’s Ethereum FXRP/RLUSD market.

Newly introduced loans could continue above the 90% utilization target while funds remained available. Morpho’s borrowing-rate curve steepens above that point.

Sources indicate that balances and allocation capacity could move before execution. The dashboard and API readings were captured about two minutes apart.

Industry observers note that the market bar uses Morpho’s displayed 87.45% utilization as its borrowed share. The available-funds bar enlarges the unborrowed segment. In the zoom, the first 20.3% represents 207,480.83 RLUSD divided by 1,022,276.09 RLUSD from Morpho’s liquidity API. Labels round the underlying values.

Balances and allocation capacity could move before execution. The dashboard and API readings were captured about two minutes apart.

Sources indicate that the 90% mark is the reference point for Morpho’s interest-rate model. Borrowing can continue above that level while funds are available, with a steeper rate curve above the target.

If Sentora takes unborrowed RLUSD out of the market while debt stays constant, utilization rises, and the variable rate can climb without anyone taking out a fresh loan. Adding supply with debt unchanged gives latest borrowers more room and can ease rates for existing borrowers.

In a recent development, who notes long EV road trips mean hours at charging stations? BMW drove the new i3 for over 3 days, covering nearly 3,700 miles, and it took less than 3 hours of charging.

BMW put the i3 to the ultimate test of efficiency, charging speed, and long-distance EV capability on a nearly 3,700-mile Pan-European journey.

Sources indicate that the Paneurpeana, as it’s called, is considered the benchmark for range and charging speed. The route begins at the North Cape in Norway, the northernmost point of continental Europe you can reach by car, and ends in Tarifa, Spain, the southernmost point of mainland Europe.

BMW drove the newly introduced i3 50 xDrive for a total of 3,658 miles (5,886.7 km) across eight countries and spent just 2 hours, 45 minutes, and 54 seconds charging at an average of 275 kW.

The performance beat the previous record by more than seven hours, according to Mike Reichelt, head of BMW’s Neue Klasse.

BMW said the charging points were not predetermined and that it had to account for external factors such as weather and traffic jams.

The newly introduced i3 was impressively efficient during the trip, consuming an average of just 12.5 kWh per 100 km, beating its official WLTP combined energy consumption of 18-13.4 kWh/100 km.

BMW stated the trip took 3 days, 2 hours, and 41 minutes, with an average speed of 79.7 km/h, and that the i3 was charged exclusively at public charging points across national charging networks.

The vehicle was driven at all times by a single driver and was not modified in any way, in terms of hardware or software, from the standard i3 available for purchase.

BMW’s latest i3 uses a 108.7 kWh battery and Gen6 eDrive system that provides a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

With a drag coefficient of just 0.21, the new i3 is the most aerodynamically efficient BMW vehicle to date.

In the US, BMW remarked the fresh 2027 i3 50 xDrive will offer an EPA-estimated driving range of up to 468 miles.

It has been revealed that with an 800V architecture, the electric sedan can add nearly 262 miles (423 km) of range (WLTP) in about 10 minutes at DC fast-charging speeds up to 400 kW. In the US, the i3 has a built-in NACS port.

Very reasonable. I've been with NK iX3 from Spain to Estonia and the experience is real - low consumption, great comfort and really fast charging. And there are more and more high speed chargers every month.

In a recent development, like the fresh iX3, the i3 features BMW’s Neue Klasse interior design. The setup consists of BMW’s massive 43″ Panoramic Vision display that spans the base of the windshield and a 17.9″ floating central infotainment display.

The latest BMW i3 50 xDrive is on sale in Germany starting at €65,900 with a WLTP range of up to 566 miles (912 km).

In the US, the 2027 BMW i3 50 xDrive and 2027 iX3 50 xDrive are available to order, both starting at $61,500.
